title: Python for problem solving
learning_objectives: Explain the mechanism behind Python for problem solving.
Implement or demonstrate: Build a frequency map, FIFO queue and priority queue.
Identify the failure mode and explain the verification evidence.
concepts: Use list, dict, set, tuple, deque and heapq. Python lists support amortized O(1) append, but popping the front shifts items. Dictionaries require hashable keys.
worked_example: A queue uses deque.popleft rather than list.pop(0).
common_pitfall: Mutating a list while iterating can skip items.

Demonstrate one normal and one boundary/failure case.

title: Big-O and amortized analysis
learning_objectives: Explain the mechanism behind Big-O and amortized analysis.
Implement or demonstrate: Compare counts for linear scan and unordered pairs at n=10 and n=20.
Identify the failure mode and explain the verification evidence.
concepts: Count work as input size grows; distinguish worst, average and amortized bounds. Nested loops are not necessarily quadratic if the inner pointer advances monotonically. Auxiliary space excludes input/output unless stated.
worked_example: Doubling n roughly doubles a linear scan but quadruples a full pair enumeration.
common_pitfall: Time measurements alone cannot prove asymptotic bounds.

Implement or demonstrate: Implement recursive prefix sum and iterative equivalent; compare stack costs.
